questions.question: For which film did Asha Bhosle win the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Award in the Best Playback Singer Female category in 2002?
questions.solution:
Asha Bhosle won the IIFA Best Female Playback Singer award in 2002 for the song 'Radha Kaise Na Jale' from the Academy Award-nominated film Lagaan.

Note: This track, composed by A.R. Rahman, is celebrated for its classical touch and playful chemistry between the lead characters.

questions.question: Which of the following playback singers is the recipient of the Karnataka Ratna Award 2005?
questions.solution:
Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, the doyen of the Kirana Gharana, was honored with the Karnataka Ratna in 2005. This is the highest civilian honor of the state of Karnataka.

Fact: He is one of the few musicians to receive both the Karnataka Ratna and the Bharat Ratna (2008).

questions.question: Which playback singer was honoured with the Nightingale of Asia Award in 1987?
questions.solution:
Asha Bhosle was honored with the Nightingale of Asia award in 1987 in Tokyo, Japan.

Legacy: Known for her incredible versatility, she holds the Guinness World Record for the most studio recordings (singles) in music history.

questions.question: Which singer from Assam was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019?
questions.solution:
Bhupen Hazarika, the legendary 'Bard of Brahmaputra', was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019.

Contribution: He was a lyricist, musician, and filmmaker who brought the folk music of Assam and Northeast India to the global stage.

questions.question: AR Rehman, Gulzar and _____ won the 52nd annual Grammy Award for the best motion picture song ‘Jai ho’.
questions.solution:
At the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards, the song 'Jai Ho' from Slumdog Millionaire won Best Compilation Soundtrack and Best Song Written for Visual Media. The winners included A.R. Rahman, Gulzar, and Tanvi Shah.

Fact: Tanvi Shah is the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award.

questions.question: Gangu bai Hangal and Prabha Atre were exponents of the ___________ Gharana.
questions.solution:
Gangubai Hangal and Dr. Prabha Atre were two of the most eminent female vocalists of the Kirana Gharana.

Gharana Style: This school of music, founded by Abdul Karim Khan, is known for its extreme focus on Swara (note) clarity and emotional depth.

questions.question: Ali Akbar Khan was associated with which of the following gharanas?
questions.solution:
Ustad Ali Akbar Khan belonged to the Maihar Gharana, founded by his father, Acharya Allauddin Khan.

Instrument: He was a virtuoso of the Sarod and played a pivotal role in popularizing Indian classical music in the United States.

questions.question: Gangubai Hangal belonged to the ________.
questions.solution: Gangubai Hangal, a Padma Vibhushan recipient, was a staunch practitioner of the Kirana Gharana. She was known for her deep, powerful voice which broke traditional gender barriers in Hindustani classical music.

questions.question: Ishwari Prasad is credited to have introduced the ________ Gharana of Kathak.
questions.solution:
Ishwari Prasad is the legendary ancestor credited with the origin of the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak.

History: He was a devotee of Lord Krishna, and his lineage eventually led to the development of the sophisticated style practiced by Pandit Birju Maharaj.

questions.question: Who among the following is the world renowned exponent of the bamboo flute?
questions.solution:
Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a world-renowned maestro of the Bansuri (bamboo flute) in the Hindustani classical tradition.

Note: Unlike many other classical musicians, he did not come from a musical family and learned secretly from his father's disapproval.

questions.question: Mohan Veena player, Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the ____________ Award in the year 1994.
questions.solution:
Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, the creator of the Mohan Veena (a modified slide guitar), won the Grammy Award in 1994 for his album 'A Meeting by the River'.

Collaboration: He won this prestigious award alongside American guitarist Ry Cooder.

questions.question: Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar was a ___________ player of profound depth, favouring sparse and slow realisations of ragas.
questions.solution: Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar was a master of the Rudra Veena. He was instrumental in bringing this ancient, meditative instrument to the modern concert stage, emphasizing the Dhrupad style of slow melodic development.

questions.question: Who among the following is a Sarod player popularly known as ‘Sarod Samrat’?
questions.solution:
Ustad Amjad Ali Khan Bangash is widely known by the title 'Sarod Samrat' (Emperor of Sarod).

Legacy: He represents the sixth generation of the Bangash lineage and has innovated the instrument to play complex vocal-style compositions.

questions.question: The famous santoor player Pandit Shivkumar Sharma received the ________________________ in the year 1986.
questions.solution:
Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, the man who gave the Santoor a classical status, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1986.

Impact: He transformed a 100-stringed Kashmiri folk instrument into a lead instrument for Indian classical ragas.

questions.question: Classical Sarod player, Amjad Ali Khan was awarded ____________ in 2001 by the Government of India.
questions.solution:
Ustad Amjad Ali Khan was conferred with the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, in 2001.

Awards: He is also a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the UNESCO Gandhi Medal.

questions.question: Harmonium player, Tulsidas Borkar, was awarded with the ___________ in 2016.
questions.solution:
The renowned Harmonium player Tulsidas Borkar was honored with the Padma Shri in 2016 for his lifelong contribution to Indian classical music.

Innovation: He is credited with technical modifications to the harmonium to make it better suited for solo classical performances.

questions.question: Which famous santoor player was honoured with the Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan Award in 1998?
questions.solution: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was honored with the Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan Award in 1998. This award, instituted by the Sarod maestro Amjad Ali Khan in memory of his father, recognizes masters of classical music.

questions.question: Ali Akbar Khan is known for playing the ________.
questions.solution: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan is synonymous with the Sarod. He was famously described by Yehudi Menuhin as "the greatest musician in the world." He founded the Ali Akbar College of Music in California.

questions.question: In 2002, Zakir Hussain became the youngest percussionist to be honoured with which award?
questions.solution:
In 2002, Ustad Zakir Hussain was awarded the Padma Bhushan. At that time, he was the youngest percussionist to receive this high civilian honor.

Note: He is a global icon of the Tabla and has collaborated with artists across genres worldwide.

questions.question: Hariprasad Chaurasia, an Indian flutist in the Hindustani classical tradition, was awarded with which of the following awards in 2000?
questions.solution:
Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in the year 2000.

Recognition: This followed his Padma Bhushan in 1992, highlighting his status as the premier flautist of India.

questions.question: The Maharashtra Bhushan was conferred upon _________________ in the year 2002.
questions.solution:
Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was conferred with the Maharashtra Bhushan award in 2002.

Context: Although born in Karnataka, he spent much of his musical life in Pune, Maharashtra, where he founded the Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav.

questions.question: Pandit Omkar Nath Thakur was a student of ____________.
questions.solution:
Pandit Omkarnath Thakur, a legendary Hindustani vocalist, was a prominent disciple of Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

Legacy: He was the first dean of the music faculty at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) and was known for his dramatic, emotional singing style.

questions.question: Who among the following was the youngest instrumentalist to be awarded the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award of India in 2002?
questions.solution:
Ustad Zakir Hussain became the youngest instrumentalist to receive the Padma Bhushan in 2002.

Update: He later received the Padma Vibhushan in 2023, solidifying his place as a living legend of the Tabla.

questions.question: Sitar maestro, Pandit Ravi Shankar was awarded which of the following awards by the Government of India in 1999?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ravi Shankar was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999.

Fact: He was a 5-time Grammy Award winner and is credited with introducing the Sitar to the Western world through his association with The Beatles.

questions.question: Which of the following awards was won by Lata Mangeshkar in the year 2001?
questions.solution:
Lata Mangeshkar, the 'Nightingale of India', was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

Career: She recorded songs in over 36 languages and was the second vocalist (after M.S. Subbulakshmi) to receive this honor.
